title: Flood (Season of Plenty) mints and dumps Beans sized by instantaneous well reserves and swaps with zero slippage, enabling flash-loan over-mint + sandwich of stalkholder proceeds
description: During a Flood, SeasonFacet.gm() -> calcCaseIdandUpdate() -> LibFlood.handleRain() takes the else (flood) branch and calls getWellsByDeltaB(), which derives each well's deltaB from LibDeltaB.currentDeltaB(well) -> IWell(well).getReserves(). These are the INSTANTANEOUS spot reserves of the Well, not the manipulation-resistant cumulative-pump TWAP that the sunrise mint uses (LibWellMinting.twaDeltaB / readTwaReserves). calculateSopPerWell() converts that instantaneous positive deltaB directly into the Bean amount to mint, then sopWell() does C.bean().mint(this, sopBeans) followed by IWell(well).swapFrom(bean, sopToken, sopBeans, 0, this, type(uint256).max) — minAmountOut hardcoded to 0 and deadline to max. The non-Bean proceeds (e.g. WETH) are distributed to Stalkholders via rewardSop(). Because the entire SOP size and the swap price both come from the live, single-block-manipulable Well state, a flood season is a deterministic, permissionlessly-triggerable MEV event: (1) an attacker who pushes the Well's Bean reserve down (raising instantaneous deltaB) immediately before the sunrise tx inflates sopBeans, and (2) the zero-minAmountOut swap can be sandwiched so the attacker buys the dumped Beans cheaply / sells the scarce non-Bean token, extracting value that should have become stalkholder plenty. The flood is triggerable by anyone via the permissionless sunrise/gm() once Beanstalk has been Oversaturated for a season, so the attacker controls the timing.
impact: Stalkholders receive materially less SOP plenty than the Flood mints; the shortfall is captured by the MEV/sandwich actor. Combined with instantaneous-reserve sizing, an attacker can also force a larger Bean mint+dump than the protocol intends, deepening the post-flood depeg. Value-at-risk per flood scales with Well liquidity and the depth of the reserve skew; on a deep Bean:ETH well a single flood can leak a large fraction of the SOP proceeds. No privileged access required.

ite.intent: Capture the non-Bean proceeds of a Flood that are meant to be distributed to Stalkholders, and force a larger Bean mint+dump than intended
ite.technique: Permissionlessly trigger the Flood via sunrise/gm(); pre-skew the Well so currentDeltaB (instantaneous getReserves) over-sizes the SOP mint; sandwich the minAmountOut=0 swapFrom in LibFlood.sopWell
ite.evasion: SOP intentionally uses instantaneous deltaB and a 0-slippage market sell; there is no commit/TWAP guard or minimum-out on the protocol's own swap, so the manipulation leaves no revert path

ice_chain.corrupted_state: sopBeans (Bean amount minted+sold) and the realized swap price / amountOut of WETH credited to s.sys.sop.sops[rainStart][well]
ice_chain.impact: Stalkholder SOP plenty is under-credited and the Bean depeg is deepened; the difference is extracted by the attacker
ice_chain.consumer_function: LibFlood.rewardSop -> s.sys.sop.sops[...] consumed by LibFlood.balanceOfPlenty / ClaimFacet plenty claims
ice_chain.exploit_path: permissionless sunrise/gm() during an Oversaturated streak -> handleRain flood branch -> getWellsByDeltaB() reads instantaneous getReserves() -> calculateSopPerWell sizes sopBeans -> sopWell() mint+swapFrom(minOut=0) on the attacker-skewed well -> reduced amountOut -> rewardSop credits less plenty to stalkholders
